chunks: DEMO UNIVERSITY - MEDICAL LEAVE AND ATTENDANCE POLICY [SANDBOX DEMO DOCUMENT - NOT A REAL INSTITUTIONAL POLICY] Document ID: POL-ATT-2024 Version: 3.2 Effective Date: August 1, 2024 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 1: ATTENDANCE REQUIREMENTS 1.1 All students must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in each course to be eligible to appear for semester examinations. 1.2 Students with attendance between 65% and 75% may be allowed to appear for examinations upon approval of the Dean of Academic Affairs, provided valid reasons are documented. 1.3 Students with attendance below 65% will be considered debarred from examinations unless special dispensation is granted under Section 4 (Medical Emergency Provisions). 1.4 Attendance is calculated based on the total number of classes held in each course. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 2: MEDICAL LEAVE PROVISIONS 2.1 Students who are absent due to illness, injury, or other documented medical conditions may apply for medical leave. 2.2 Medical leave applications must be submitted within 5 working days of returning to the institution. 2.3 Required documentation for medical leave: a) Medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner b) Hospital discharge summary (if hospitalized) c) Any supporting documents as deemed necessary by the Medical Officer 2.4 Medical leave of up to 30 days per semester may be granted without affecting the student's academic standing, subject to documentation. 2.5 For hospitalization cases: Students hospitalized for more than 2 consecutive days are eligible for medical leave covering the entire hospitalization period plus 3 days of recovery. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 3: ATTENDANCE CONDONATION 3.1 Students with medical leave absences will have those days condoned (not counted against attendance). 3.2 After condonation, if attendance meets the 75% threshold, the student is eligible for examinations without restriction. 3.3 If post-condonation attendance is between 65-74%, the student may appear for examinations with a written undertaking from a parent/guardian. 3.4 The condonation process must be initiated through the Student Services Portal within 10 days of returning from medical leave. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 4: MEDICAL EMERGENCY PROVISIONS 4.1 In cases of sudden medical emergencies (accidents, acute illness requiring emergency hospitalization), special provisions apply. 4.2 Students unable to attend classes or examinations due to a verified medical emergency will be granted: a) Full attendance condonation for the emergency period b) Right to sit for deferred/make-up examinations c) Extension of assignment submission deadlines 4.3 Verification process: Emergency medical leaves require submission of: - Hospital admission records - Discharge summary from treating physician - Medical certificate specifying dates of incapacity 4.4 Emergency medical provisions must be invoked within 7 days of the student's return to campus. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 5: CONDONATION LIMITS 5.1 Maximum condonable absence per semester: 15% of total classes 5.2 Attendance after condonation must not fall below 60% 5.3 A student may not invoke medical condonation in consecutive semesters without review by the Academic Committee ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ DISCLAIMER: DEMO UNIVERSITY - EXAM ABSENCE AND DEFERRAL POLICY [SANDBOX DEMO DOCUMENT - NOT A REAL INSTITUTIONAL POLICY] Document ID: POL-EXAM-2024 Version: 2.1 Effective Date: August 1, 2024 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 1: GENERAL PROVISIONS 1.1 All students are expected to appear for scheduled examinations. Missing an examination without prior approval or valid documented reason may result in a grade of zero for that examination. 1.2 This policy recognizes that genuine emergencies may prevent students from appearing for examinations. 1.3 The university provides mechanisms for exam deferral in documented cases of medical emergencies, bereavement, or other exceptional circumstances. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 2: GROUNDS FOR EXAM DEFERRAL 2.1 MEDICAL EMERGENCY Students absent due to documented medical emergencies may request exam deferral. Medical emergency includes: - Hospitalization (any duration) - Acute illness requiring bed rest certified by a physician - Accidents resulting in physical incapacitation - Emergency surgery or medical procedures 2.2 BEREAVEMENT Death of an immediate family member (parent, sibling, spouse, child). Maximum deferral period: 7 days from the date of bereavement. 2.3 NATURAL DISASTER OR FORCE MAJEURE Events beyond the student's control affecting their ability to appear. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 3: APPLICATION PROCESS FOR EXAM DEFERRAL 3.1 Students must submit a deferral request through the Academic Affairs Portal. 3.2 Deferral requests must be submitted BEFORE the examination date if possible, or within 48 hours after the missed examination. 3.3 If the student is hospitalized and unable to submit the request personally, a parent, guardian, or authorized representative may submit on their behalf. 3.4 Required documents for medical deferral: a) Medical certificate from a registered practitioner (mandatory) b) Hospital discharge summary (mandatory for hospitalization cases) c) Admission records (if available) 3.5 Incomplete applications will be rejected. Students will be notified of missing documents and given 5 days to provide them. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 4: EXAM DATE CHANGE PROVISIONS 4.1 The university reserves the right to change examination dates due to: - Scheduling conflicts - External events (natural disasters, public emergencies) - Technical or administrative reasons 4.2 In case of exam date change, the university will notify students with at least 24 hours' notice. 4.3 IMPORTANT: If an exam date is changed to a date within a student's approved medical leave period, the student's deferral request is automatically extended to cover the new date. 4.4 Students who were already on approved medical leave when an exam date change is announced should be automatically rescheduled. Students should confirm this with the Academic Affairs office. 4.5 If the changed exam date creates a conflict with an ongoing medical absence, the student must notify the Academic Affairs office within 12 hours of the announcement. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 5: MAKE-UP EXAMINATION SCHEDULE 5.1 Make-up examinations for approved deferrals are conducted 2-3 weeks after the original exam date. 5.2 Students who receive exam deferral approval will be notified of the make-up exam schedule within 5 business days. 5.3 Make-up examination format and difficulty are equivalent to the original examination. 5.4 Only one deferral is permitted per course per semester. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 6: ATTENDANCE ELIGIBILITY FOR DEFERRAL 6.1 Students must have a minimum of 60% attendance (after

weeks after the original exam date. 5.2 Students who receive exam deferral approval will be notified of the make-up exam schedule within 5 business days. 5.3 Make-up examination format and difficulty are equivalent to the original examination. 5.4 Only one deferral is permitted per course per semester. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ SECTION 6: ATTENDANCE ELIGIBILITY FOR DEFERRAL 6.1 Students must have a minimum of 60% attendance (after medical condonation) to be eligible for exam deferral. 6.2 Students with attendance below 60% even after condonation are not eligible for exam deferral and must re-register for the course. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ DISCLAIMER: This is a sandbox/demo document created for the RAAHAT prototype. It does not represent any real institution's policies.

DEMO UNIVERSITY - MEDICAL LEAVE REQUEST PROCEDURE [SANDBOX DEMO DOCUMENT - NOT A REAL INSTITUTIONAL POLICY] Document ID: PROC-ML-2024 Version: 1.5 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ HOW TO APPLY FOR MEDICAL LEAVE Step 1: Collect medical documents - Get a discharge summary from the hospital (for hospitalization) - Get a medical certificate from your treating physician - Collect any additional supporting documents Step 2: Submit application - Go to Student Services Portal (academic.demouniversity.edu/portal) - Navigate to "Leave Applications" > "Medical Leave" - Fill in the required details - Upload scanned copies of all documents - Submit application Step 3: Verification - The Medical Officer will verify the documents within 2 business days - You will receive an email confirmation of receipt Step 4: Approval / Rejection - Approved: Your leave is recorded, attendance is condoned - Rejected: You will receive reasons and may resubmit with correct documents Step 5: Follow-up for exam deferral (if applicable) - If your leave covers an examination date, separately apply for exam deferral - Navigate to "Exam Requests" > "Medical Deferral" - Reference your approved medical leave application ID IMPORTANT NOTES: - Keep originals of all documents for physical verification if requested - Email submissions are NOT accepted; use the online portal only - Applications submitted after the 5-day deadline require special approval from the Dean ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ CONTACT Student Services: studentservices@demouniversity.edu (DEMO) Academic Affairs: academics@demouniversity.edu (DEMO) Medical Officer: medicalofficer@demouniversity.edu (DEMO) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ DISCLAIMER: This is a sandbox/demo document. FINANCIAL OBLIGATIONS DURING MEDICAL LEAVE - GUIDANCE DOCUMENT [SANDBOX DEMO DOCUMENT] ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ MANAGING FINANCIAL COMMITMENTS DURING MEDICAL EMERGENCIES This document provides general guidance (not financial advice) on managing financial obligations during a period of medical incapacitation. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ RENT OBLIGATIONS 1. Most landlords understand genuine medical emergencies. 2. Communicate proactively with your landlord. 3. Request a brief extension (typically 5-7 days). 4. Provide documentation of hospitalization. 5. Many landlords will accommodate if notified in advance. 6. Check rental agreement for late payment clauses. PRIORITY: HIGH - Rent is a critical obligation affecting housing security. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ CREDIT CARD OBLIGATIONS 1. Contact your credit card issuer's customer service immediately. 2. Explain the medical emergency and request a temporary extension. 3. Most major card issuers have hardship programs. 4. Request: waiver of late fees due to medical emergency. 5. Provide documentation if requested. 6. Minimum payments should be prioritized over full payments. PRIORITY: HIGH - Late payments affect credit score significantly. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ LOAN EMIs 1. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) guidelines allow moratorium requests for genuine hardship. 2. Contact your loan servicer within 5 days of the emergency. 3. EMI moratorium typically covers 1-3 months. 4. Interest continues to accrue during moratorium. 5. Documentation required: hospitalization proof. PRIORITY: MEDIUM - Banks typically have structured relief programs. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ PAYMENT PRIORITIZATION FRAMEWORK TIER 1 (Critical - Never miss): - Rent (housing security) - Utility bills (power, water) TIER 2 (High - Contact for extension): - Credit card minimum payments - Loan EMIs TIER 3 (Medium - Usually flexible): - Subscriptions - Non-essential payments ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ DISCLAIMER: This is a sandbox/demo document. Not financial advice. Always consult a qualified financial advisor for personal financial decisions.

HEALTHCO INSURANCE - CLAIM REQUIREMENTS AND CHECKLIST [SANDBOX DEMO DOCUMENT - NOT A REAL INSURANCE POLICY] Document: HC-CLAIM-REQ-2024 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ HOSPITALIZATION CLAIM CHECKLIST Before submitting your claim, ensure you have ALL of the following: □ DISCHARGE SUMMARY (MANDATORY) - Without this, the claim CANNOT be processed - Must include diagnosis, admission date, discharge date - Must be signed by treating physician on hospital letterhead □ ADMISSION NOTE (MANDATORY) - Initial assessment and reason for admission - Time and date of admission □ Original hospital bills (for reimbursement claims) □ Policy holder's government ID □ Completed HealthCo Claim Form (Form HC-2024-01) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ WHY IS THE DISCHARGE SUMMARY MANDATORY? The discharge summary is required because: 1. It confirms the patient was actually hospitalized 2. It validates the duration of hospitalization 3. It provides the official medical diagnosis 4. It confirms the treatment was medically necessary 5. It is the primary document used to assess claim validity Missing discharge summary = automatic claim rejection. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ HOW TO OBTAIN A DISCHARGE SUMMARY 1. Request from the hospital at the time of discharge 2. If not received at discharge, contact the hospital's Medical Records department 3. Most hospitals can provide discharge summary within 24-48 hours of request 4. Some hospitals provide digital copies via their patient portal ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ FILING DEADLINES - Emergency hospitalization: File within 30 days of discharge - Planned hospitalization: File within 15 days of discharge - Late filing: Subject to a 10% penalty; claims older than 60 days may be rejected ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ DISCLAIMER: SANDBOX demo document.
